gaps: The exam is multiple choice (Scrum lecture 1, slide 5: "Exam: MC (combined with Lean)"). The number of questions and the time are not stated. The exam simulation copies the teacher's test exam: 20 questions in 30 minutes.
Scrum lectures 2-4 are not in the folder. The Scrum roles, events and artifacts come from the Scrum Guide 2020 (the homework of lecture 1) and from the Scrum Kahoot.
The Scrum Kahoot file has the questions and the right answers only. The wrong options in the app were written to be clearly wrong. A typo in one Kahoot answer ("print backlog item") is flagged.
Scrum lecture 1 says a Sprint is "2 weeks to 1 month"; the Scrum Guide and the Kahoot say "one month or less". Both agree it is never longer than a month.

ITIL 4 (lecture 5) only lists names and numbers. The Kahoot and public ITIL 4 Foundation material (marked "outside the course files") fill in the guiding principles and the six value chain activities.

Kanban and DevOps (lecture 6): the coffee-shop example and the videos are not text. The Kanban practices come from the Kahoot and the public Kanban Method (marked "outside the course files"). Obeya: the slide has only the title.

The Lesson 5 deck has many picture slides (roles, DMAIC, the 7 wastes, takt time, cycle time and lead time, a pizza SIPOC, a value stream map). They were read from rendered pictures, and the video slides (YouTube) have no text.
Exercise 4 (Hout enzo): the corrected answers use a simplified lead-time method that the answer key calls a classroom simplification, not a universal law.
Chapter 9 statistics (control charts, Cp/Cpk, hypothesis tests) comes from the syllabus only. No lecture slide covers it, so it may be beyond what the exam asks.

simulation.note: The exam is multiple choice (Scrum lecture 1, slide 5), but the number of questions and the time are not stated. 20 questions in 30 minutes copies the teacher's test exam. Change the numbers in the "simulation" block of exam.json.
